decisions.reason: Small volume chambers draw on the firm's core dosimetry and calibration knowledge, so it can interpret field feedback and refine the product, and dropping it would waste that absorbed know-how.
This second small-field chamber overlaps somewhat with Product B but still builds on the same detector expertise and serves growing small-field demand, so keeping it is justified for now.
The standard clinical chamber line is central to the established business and fully integrated into accredited calibration and service, making withdrawal very unlikely.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and QA workflows using closely related knowledge, so it fits the connected platform strategy.
Thimble chambers are a long-standing core competence with long clinical and regulatory life cycles, so the firm keeps the product on the market.
